Overview

ridge is an R package for fitting Ridge Regression models and selecting regularization parameters through K-fold cross-validation.

The package combines R implementations with C++ routines using Rcpp and RcppArmadillo.

Main features

  • Ridge Regression with an unpenalized intercept.
  • K-fold cross-validation over a user-defined grid of strictly positive lambda values.
  • Pooled cross-validation error and mean fold error calculations.
  • Automatic selection of the regularization parameter.
  • Visualization of cross-validation errors.
  • A one-standard-error selection rule.
  • S3 methods for fitted models and cross-validation results.

Installation

You can install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Mustapha-Labhar/ridge")

Load the package:

library(ridge)

Ridge Regression

Ridge Regression estimates the coefficients by minimizing:

𝛃̂λ=argminβ0,𝛃[∑i=1n(yi−β0−𝐱i⊤𝛃)2+λ∑j=1pβj2]. \widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_\lambda = \arg\min_{\beta_0,\boldsymbol{\beta}} \left[ \sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i-\beta_0-\mathbf{x}_i^\top\boldsymbol{\beta})^2 + \lambda\sum_{j=1}^{p}\beta_j^2 \right].

The intercept is not penalized.

Example: fitting a model 

set.seed(123)

x <- matrix(rnorm(200), ncol = 2)
y <- 2 + 3 * x[, 1] - x[, 2] + rnorm(100)

model <- ridge_fit(x, y, lambda = 1)

model
coef(model)
fitted(model)
residuals(model)

The fitted model has class ridge_model and supports the following S3 methods:

  • print()
  • coef()
  • fitted()
  • residuals()
  • predict()

Cross-validation

The ridge_cv() function performs K-fold cross-validation over a grid of candidate regularization parameters.

lambda_grid <- 10^seq(-3, 2, length.out = 50)

cv_result <- ridge_cv(
  x,
  y,
  lambda_grid = lambda_grid,
  k = 5,
  seed = 123
)

cv_result$best_lambda
cv_result$best_mse

Cross-validation criteria

The package calculates two complementary criteria.

The pooled cross-validation error is:

CVpooled(λ)=1n∑k=1K∑i∈Vk(yi−ŷi(−k))2. CV_{\mathrm{pooled}}(\lambda) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=1}^{K} \sum_{i\in V_k} (y_i-\widehat y_i^{(-k)})^2.

The mean fold cross-validation error is:

CVfold(λ)=1K∑k=1KEk(λ), CV_{\mathrm{fold}}(\lambda) = \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} E_k(\lambda),

where Ek(λ)E_k(\lambda) is the mean squared prediction error in validation fold kk.

The best_lambda returned by ridge_cv() minimizes the pooled cross-validation error.

Visualization 

plot(cv_result)

The plot provides two selection criteria:

  • lambda_min: minimizes the mean fold cross-validation error.
  • lambda_1se: selects the largest lambda whose mean fold error is within one estimated standard error of the minimum.

These criteria are based on the mean fold errors and may differ from best_lambda, which uses the pooled criterion.

The plotting method invisibly returns the selected parameters:

selected_parameters <- plot(cv_result)

selected_parameters

Prediction

New observations can be supplied to predict():

new_data <- matrix(
  c(0.5, -0.2,
    1.0,  0.3),
  ncol = 2,
  byrow = TRUE
)

predict(model, newdata = new_data)

Implementation

The package uses:

  • R for the public interface and model methods.
  • C++ for computational routines.
  • Rcpp and RcppArmadillo for the interface between R and C++ and matrix computations.

The intercept is excluded from the Ridge penalty.

Tests and quality control

The package includes automated tests using testthat.

Run the tests with:

devtools::test()

Check the package with:

devtools::check()
